observations.finding: Cell density markedly reduced vs DMSO confluent monolayer (f_932e066d9dc7). Treated fields sparse with isolated cells/clusters and large empty background at identical contrast. This is not in top_deviations but quantified as cells_measured 230 at 0.3uM and 137 at 3.0uM vs dense DMSO; lower count at 3.0uM indicates dose-dependent loss/proliferation block.

Beta-tubulin (green in composite, no grayscale separate) strongly brighter and more heterogeneous vs DMSO diffuse perinuclear network. Treated shows dense bundles, bright focal asters/monopolar-like spindles and yellow (green+red) mitotic rounded cells with high local contrast. More pronounced at both 0.3uM (f_74075488e249,f_fb29d6b05f4a) and 3.0uM (f_81288dce1fd4,f_d7ae853e3eb2) under identical contrast = real increase.

Agrees with tub_mean z +42.1 (0.762 vs 0.247) and +38.9 (0.723 vs 0.247), tub_std z +77.4 (0.552 vs 0.121) and +69.7 (0.51 vs 0.121), tub_glcm_contrast z +154.7 (0.013 vs 0.002) and +121.7 (0.010 vs 0.002) at 0.3uM and 3.0uM = increased total polymer and texture heterogeneity/bundling.

DNA (blue) - nuclei less round/regular vs DMSO round-oval uniform nuclei. Many irregular, indented, bilobed/multilobed and condensed mitotic chromosomes in rounded cells; no massive polyploid giant nuclei. Occasional micronuclei/fragmented DAPI at 3.0uM.

Agrees with nuc_solidity z -28.9 (0.953 vs 0.972) at 0.3uM and -39.8 (0.945 vs 0.972) at 3.0uM and nuc_form_factor z -14.4 (0.845 vs 0.911) and -18.1 (0.828 vs 0.911) = decreased solidity/circularity = irregular nuclei. Stronger defect at 3.0uM.
F-actin (red) brighter, spiky peripheral ruffles and cortical contraction in rounded mitotic cells vs DMSO thin peripheral stress fibers. Increased heterogeneity and contrast.

Agrees with act_mean z +15.6 (0.53 vs 0.274) and +13.3 (0.492 vs 0.274), act_std z +17.9 (0.181 vs 0.07) and +13.8 (0.156 vs 0.07), act_glcm_contrast z +16.8 (0.003 vs 0.001) and +10.4 (0.003 vs 0.001) - all strong increases.

Phenotype consistent across both low and high concentration fields: mitotic arrest phenotype with tubulin hyper-polymerization/bundling, irregular nuclei, actin cortical remodeling; not a pure actin loss or tubulin loss.

central cluster with dense green microtubule bundles/spindles and irregular blue nuclei; same pattern at 3.0uM

data.note: Epothilone B (PubChem CID 448013, Patupilone CHEMBL94657, Tubulin stabiliser) was correctly identified as Microtubule stabilizers (p=0.96). Phenotype across 4 doses (0.01-3 µM) showed dose-dependent tubulin polymer increase (tub_mean z +2.7→+42.1, rho +0.80; tub_glcm_contrast z +5.5→+154.7), nuclear irregularity (nuc_solidity rho -1.0, z -3.8→-39.8) and cell loss, visually confirmed as bright bundled microtubules/mitotic arrest - opposite to destabilizer expectation. NSC vote unanimous 4/4 with 0.97-0.97 similarity to reference stabilizers docetaxel/taxol at matched doses (e4, e11). This matches literature: Kamath & Jordan 2003 showed suppression of microtubule dynamics by epothilone B is associated with mitotic arrest (PMID 14522931), and recent structural work on epothilone-B-induced stabilization (PMID 41224993) and reviews of stabilizer phenotypes (PMID 24491636).

reflection.text:
Unblinded truth: epothilone B, ChEMBL Tubulin stabiliser - call Microtubule stabilizers (p=0.96) was correct.

What the evidence got right and why:

1. **Acquisition strategy captured the dose-dependent tubulin gain-of-signal:** Starting with high dose w_56c0ae0535 (3 uM, e2) and mid dose w_2e25395163 (0.3 uM, e3) showed extreme microtubule texture/bundling signal: tub_glcm_contrast z=+121.7 to +154.7, tub_std z=+69.7 to +77.4, tub_mean z=+42.1. This direction is opposite to a destabilizer which would decrease tubulin intensity/texture. The low dose w_a15719a464 (0.01 uM, e6) was near baseline (z~+5) and intermediate w_b414b296e0 (0.1 uM, e7) was z~+28-33, giving the onset curve visualized by dose_response e8 rho=+0.80 for tub_mean and e10 rho=-1.00 (p=0) for nuc_solidity. That monotonic increase in tubulin signal with irregular nuclei was the core discriminator.

2. **Atlas comparison was unanimous and consistent with visual phenotype:** Initial NSC vote 2/2 (e4) and final 4/4 (e11) for Microtubule stabilizers, with k-neighbours 5/10 stabilizers. describe_phenotype e5 on 4 fields independently reported density similar vs DMSO and candidate Microtubule stabilizers with dense bundled tubulin, directly confirming the quantitative z-scores were not an artifact of cell-count loss or segmentation.

3. **Identity check closes the loop:** lookup_compound e14/e15 PubChem CID 448013 / ChEMBL CHEMBL94657 mechanisms: Tubulin stabiliser, name and BBBC021 structure agree with unblinding. Literature returned in this run is concordant: epothilone B as microtubule stabilizer associated with suppression of microtubule dynamics and mitotic arrest PMID 14522931, and in situ structural mechanism for CNS axon regeneration PMID 41224993, plus other epothilone B microtubule-stabilizer reports PMID 41663006, PMID 41519196, PMID 29348323. General microtubule stabilizer phenotype context PMID 24491636.

What was ambiguous / could have misled and what we missed:

- **Single-replicate wells and underpowered dose-response p-values:** list_available_experiments e1 left only 4 wells to sample 8 doses (0.001-3 uM). We sampled 4 doses but each n=1. e8 rho=+0.80 p=0.2 for tub_mean and e9 rho=-0.80 p=0.2 for cell_count are not significant by p-value due to n=4. We did not over-rely on p-values and instead used magnitude and consistency across 4 independent doses plus e10 perfect monotonicity for nuc_solidity to justify 0.96. Single-replicate remains the main limitation noted in review.

- **Neighbour classes:** k-neighbour classes included Protein degradation (2/10) and Cholesterol-lowering (1/10) in e4/e11. These could distract, but they did not explain the primary directional tubulin increase and were correctly treated as distant neighbours vs unanimous NSC vote. No contradictory tubulin decrease evidence (hypothesis_history correctly set Microtubule destabilizers 0.01 with contradicting e2,e3,e4,e5,e8,e11).

- **Cell count trend:** e9 rho=-0.80 suggests modest toxicity/mitotic arrest, and e2 n=137 vs e6 n=433 supports loss at high dose, but density similar vs DMSO in e5 shows this is not gross cytotoxicity at screening density - consistent with mitotic arrest rather than non-specific killing - we did not over-interpret it as a separate MoA.

No evidence was ignored; acquisition choices (high -> mid -> low -> intermediate) efficiently mapped both maximal effect and onset without needing the 8-dose full curve for this high-confidence stabilizer phenotype. This is a cell-biology screening interpretation only, not clinical advice.
